modules.text: The platform covers PLM, order and inventory management, native EDI, warehouse management, financials, and AI-powered analytics in one system.
Module list includes Ecommerce Integrations and AI Support (Ai2000 University).
PLM module covers design, tech pack (BOM + grading), sample (lab dips + fittings), costing, production (PO + factory tracking) and ship (QC + delivery), with a vendor portal.

PLM supports category-specific attributes for apparel, footwear (size run matrices, widths, lasts, tooling) and home goods (multi-component assemblies, dimensions and cube, packaging and carton specs).
Footwear page describes native warehouse operations including receiving, pick, pack, ship and cycle counts, and a B2B portal.
The platform includes AI Upload tools, AI University, AI 24/7 Training & Support, AI-powered Business Analytics and an AI-Reporting tool.

customer_segments.text: Purpose-built for mid-market apparel and fashion brands, wholesalers, and distributors.
Serves three industries: apparel and fashion, footwear, and home goods.
Built for designers, wholesalers, manufacturers, and retailers.
Footwear business models listed include branded footwear, wholesale distribution, private label sourcing and DTC footwear.

customer_size_signals.text: Customers range from growing wholesale brands to global fashion houses.
Named brands include Michael Kors, Carolina Herrera, Oscar de la Renta, Tumi, BCBGMAXAZRIA, Anne Klein, London Fog, Nicole Miller.
Reviews page cites 300+ companies as customers.
Reviewer segments include Wholesale (201-500 employees) and Home Textiles (11-50 employees).

deployment.text: Offers a SaaS offering; described as having modern cloud architecture.
Footwear page states deployment is cloud or hybrid, with scope confirmed in the project plan.
Claims implementation targeted at one season, with full data migration and ongoing training.

integrations.text: Plugs into Gemini, OpenAI and Claude AI models.
Supports EDI and integration with 500+ trading partners.
Ecommerce integrations include Shopify and Magento, per blog; FAQ asks about Shopify and Amazon.
Supports EDI 850/856/810 documents, ASNs, labels and routing compliance.

differentiators.text: Features are built natively with no third-party integrations or extra licenses; no middleware or per-transaction EDI fees.
Company states it has been in apparel ERP since 1979 in a blog, while About page says founded 1996 (inconsistent).
Wolfpack 6 case: hours of manual weekend reporting reduced to minutes within first two weeks.
Compares itself against NetSuite, AIMS360 and Acumatica.

recent_news.text: Company rebranded A2000 Software to Ai2000, rebuilt from the ground up with AI.
Featured article (May 2026) from Founder & CEO on ERPs and AI.

gaps_or_opportunities.text: About page notes some figures are unverified placeholders (brands served, countries).
Reviewer ratings show Functionality as the lowest score (4.4) vs. Ease of Use 4.6.
